summary: Tested Multi-Level Calling/Follow-up Tracker (backend + frontend) end-to-end. All 10 pytest cases pass; UI integration on Notes tab verified for Sales and Accounts roles; reminder hook polls /api/follow-ups/upcoming from DashboardLayout as expected. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: useFollowUpReminders.isDue() uses ISO date string compared against local-timezone `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)` (UTC), while time comparison uses local hours. This date/time mismatch is mostly harmless (errs on the side of firing slightly early) but could be made consistent by deriving both from the same TZ.

Backend _compute_overdue_stages caps at admin's current_stage but iterates PAYMENT_STAGES in declared order — assumes that order matches cumulative progression. Safe today, but a sort-by-cumulative would be more defensive.
GET /api/follow-ups/upcoming scans every customer with follow_ups (no Mongo-side date filter). Fine for current scale; consider an index/$elemMatch filter as data grows.
test_credentials: admin crm@rrlbuildersanddevelopers.com/#RRLnew2026, sales sales@rrlrprojects.com/sales123, accounts accounts@rrlbuilders.com/accounts123. Test customer 6d902613-5106-4294-bc3e-b907f85127f7 (Ramya).
seed_data_creation: All TEST_-prefixed follow-ups created during testing were deleted in fixture teardown and a final cleanup pass; Ramya's follow_ups array is empty post-run (verified via GET).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_follow_ups.py covers POST/GET/DELETE/upcoming + 400 validation for invalid status/stage, 404 for unknown customer/follow-up, and role coverage (admin/sales/accounts). Frontend tracker uses data-testid='follow-up-tracker' and lives above Notes card inside Notes tab. useFollowUpReminders is mounted in DashboardLayout and was observed polling /api/follow-ups/upcoming within seconds of landing on /dashboard. Auth token is stored in sessionStorage (not localStorage).
backend_coverage: GET /api/customers/{id}/follow-ups → shape (follow_ups, overdue_stages, current_stage, all_stages, statuses) and sort order
POST validation: invalid status → 400; invalid stage_key → 400
POST create returns full entry with id/created_at/created_by/created_by_name
Persistence: created entry retrievable via GET and ordered desc by created_at
